phrase-tier: words that sit next to each other rank above words that are merely both present
(PLAN J18; 4.6).

Two notes use the words "disk" and "quota". One says "disk quota" in a row; the other mentions
them in separate sentences and is the better match for a plain AND search. With phrase_boost
(the default) the chunk holding the phrase leads. kb explain names the tier of every hit, and
the setting turns the tiers off.

  $ kb init --model fake:8
  created location $WORK/proj/.kb
  created store "default" in $WORK/proj (model fake:8)

  $ kb add $WORK/notes/scattered.md
  added data/scattered.md (2 chunks)
  $ kb add $WORK/notes/adjacent.md
  added data/adjacent.md (2 chunks)

  $ kb search 'disk quota' --mode fts
  search 1 · 3 hits
  [1] data/adjacent.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-02
  Reporting › (intro)
  # Reporting

  A disk quota alert is filed in the tracker.

  [2] data/scattered.md · updated 2026-02-01
  Storage planning: Disk and quota planning.

  [3] data/scattered.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-01
  Storage planning › (intro)
  # Storage planning

  Every disk is checked weekly. Each team keeps a quota. The disk report and the quota report
  are separate.
  search_id=1

Quotes add nothing: the phrase tier is automatic for any query of two or more words, so a
quoted query is the same search.

  $ kb search '"disk quota"' --mode fts
  search 2 · 3 hits
  [1] data/adjacent.md › (intro) · updated 2026-02-02
  ...
  search_id=2

Reverse the words and no chunk holds the phrase: the scattered note, with more matches, leads.

  $ kb search 'quota disk' --mode fts
  search 3 · 3 hits
  [1] data/scattered.md · updated 2026-02-01
  ...
  search_id=3

kb explain names the tiers (each with its row count) and the tier of every hit.

  $ kb explain 'disk quota' --mode fts
  ~ explain "disk quota" · mode fts · k 8 · settings [0-9a-f]{12}
  ...
  tiers: phrase "disk quota" (1 row) · near NEAR("disk" "quota", 8) (3 rows) · and "disk" AND "quota" (3 rows)
  lists: fts 3 rows · vec 0 rows · 3 candidates
  ...
  ~ #1  rrf [0-9.]+  data/adjacent.md › \(intro\)  \[returned as hit #1\]
  ~     fts  rank 1  tier phrase  bm25 .*
  ...
  ~ #2  rrf [0-9.]+  data/scattered.md  \[returned as hit #2\]
  ~     fts  rank 2  tier near  bm25 .*
  ...
  ~ #3  rrf [0-9.]+  data/scattered.md › \(intro\)  \[returned as hit #3\]
  ~     fts  rank 3  tier near  bm25 .*
  ...

With search.phrase_boost off the tiers go away and the plain AND order returns.

  $ kb explain 'disk quota' --mode fts --set search.phrase_boost=false
  ~ explain "disk quota" · mode fts · k 8 · settings [0-9a-f]{12}
  ...
  tiers: off (search.phrase_boost = false)
  ...
  ~ #1  rrf [0-9.]+  data/scattered.md  \[returned as hit #1\]
  ~     fts  rank 1  bm25 .*
  ...

Judge the phrase hit of the first search, then ask the log how each tier did: kb stats tiers
counts the shown hits per tier and how many were judged useful.

  $ kb feedback 1 1 --useful
  recorded: search 1 rank 1 useful=1
  $ kb stats tiers --json
  {
    "query": "tiers",
    "columns": [
      "tier",
      "results",
      "share_pct",
      "judged",
      "useful",
      "useful_rate_pct",

      "with_memory",
      "memory_useful"
    ],
    "rows": [
      {
        "avg_rank": 1,

        "memory_useful": 0,
        "results": 2,
        "share_pct": 22.2,
        "tier": "phrase",
        "useful": 1,
        "useful_rate_pct": 100,
        "with_memory": 0
      },
      {
        "avg_rank": 2.29,
        "judged": 0,
        "memory_useful": 0,
        "results": 7,
        "share_pct": 77.8,
        "tier": "near",
        "useful": 0,
